title: Anchovies, canned in olive oil, with salt, drained

content.title: About
content.content: Anchovies are small marine fish of the Engraulidae family that are commonly canned in olive oil with added salt. After cooking, the fish are drained to remove excess oil, leaving a flavorful, salty product with a delicate, melt‑in‑your‑mouth texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Anchovies have been used in Mediterranean cuisine for centuries primarily as a flavor enhancer rather than a main dish.
Canning in olive oil helps preserve the omega‑3 fatty acids that are otherwise sensitive to heat.
Salt not only boosts taste but also acts as a natural preservative, extending shelf life.
In Italy, anchovies are often served as “acquacotta” – small portions on toasted bread with tomatoes and olive oil.
Draining the oil reduces the calorie count while retaining most of the beneficial nutrients.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Anchovies provide EPA and DHA, omega‑3s that support cardiovascular health and brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: A 100‑g serving delivers about 20 g of complete protein essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and contributes to immune system regulation.

items.title: Minerals: calcium and iron
items.content: Calcium supports bone health, while iron is vital for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The product is virtually carb‑free, making it suitable for low‑carb and ketogenic diets.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The added salt can raise blood pressure; people with hypertension should limit portion size.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to seafood may experience severe reactions to anchovies.

items.title: Histamine levels
items.content: Canned fish can contain histamine, which may cause adverse symptoms in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Oil quality control
items.content: Poor‑quality olive oil can oxidize, diminishing the nutritional value of the product.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Anchovies in olive oil are commonly added to sauces (e.g., Caesar dressing), salads, pasta, pizza, and tapas. They also make a tasty snack when spread on crusty bread with a few fresh vegetables. Draining excess oil before use can lower the calorie load if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place with the lid tightly sealed. Once opened, keep the anchovies refrigerated in their original oil or a small amount of fresh olive oil, and consume within 3–5 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
